def: Skill and judgement a person uses without being able to state it fully, so that asking for the rules yields only part of what they know.
Unwanted variability in the judgements of different experts, or of one expert on different days, on identical cases.
Observing someone do their real work without directing it, to see what they actually look at, skip, check and ask.
An elicitation method in which an expert performs a real task while saying whatever passes through their mind, without explaining or justifying.
An interview technique that walks an expert through one memorable hard case, marking each decision point and what they noticed and considered.
Two near-identical cases with different outcomes, shown to an expert to elicit the difference that matters and yield a minimal test case.
A list of observable criteria, each with a few anchored levels, that lets different people or a model score the same output consistently.
A measure of agreement between two labellers that corrects for the agreement expected by chance, from 1 for perfect agreement to 0 for chance level.
A meeting in which experts who labelled independently discuss their disagreements, write rulings and update the guideline before labelling a fresh batch.
